S/RES/2832 (2026) · 2026-10-19

UN Security Council Resolution 2832 (2026)

The use of digital technologies by parties to armed conflict to commit, facilitate, enable or exacerbate violations and abuses against children

Ukraine and fragmentation · Other

Yes No Abstained
Children and armed conflictSexual violenceHuman rightsHumanitarian access and aidJustice and impunityRefugees and displacement

Official document (PDF) · Draft S/2026/815 · Meeting record S/PV.10247

United Nations S/RES/2832 (2026) Security Council Distr.: General 19 October 2026 Resolution 2832 (2026) Adopted by the Security Council at its 10247th meeting , on 19 October 2026 The Security Council , Reaffirming its resolutions 1261 (1999) , 1314 (2000) , 1379 (2001) , 1460 (2003) , 1539 (2004) , 1612 (2005) , 1882 (2009) , 1998 (2011) , 2068 (2012) , 2143 (2014) , 2225 (2015) , 2427 (2018) , 2601 (2021) , and 2764 (2024) and all relevant Statements of its President, which contribute to a comprehensive framework for addressing the protection of children affected by armed conflict, Reiterating its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations, and, in this connection, its commitment to address the widespread impact of armed conflict on children and the long-term consequences this has for durable peace, security and development, Stressing the primary role and responsibility of Governments in providing protection and relief to all children affected by armed conflict and recognizing the importance of strengthening national capacities in this regard, Recalling that all parties to armed conflict must comply strictly with the obligations applicable to them under international law for the protection of children in armed conflict, including those contained in the Geneva Conventions of 12th August 1949 and the Additional Protocols of 1977 as well as in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and its Optional Protocol on the involvement of Children in armed conflict, welcoming the steps taken by a number of Member States to make commitments to protect children affected by armed conflict, including the ratification of the Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child on the involvement of children in armed conflict, Taking note of ongoing international and regional initiatives on Children and Armed Conflict, including the international conference held in Paris in 2007 on protecting children from unlawful recruitment or use by armed forces or armed groups and the follow-up conference held in Paris in 2017, and the commitments during the conferences and further taking note of the efforts of States to foster international cooperation on countering the use of digital technologies in violations against children, including in the framework of the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime; Strengthening International Cooperation for Combatting Certain Crimes Committed by Means of Information and Communications Technology Systems and for the Sharing of Evidence in Electronic Form of Serious Crimes, Expressing deep concern at emerging trends in the increasing use of digital technologies, including social media, gaming platforms, and encrypted communication tools, by parties to armed conflict to commit, facilitate, enable or exacerbate violations and abuses against children, including recruitment and use, abduction and rape and other forms of sexual violence, Recognizing that digital technologies have the potential to be beneficial for children affected by armed conflict, including for their protection and development, for the prevention of the recruitment and use of children and of other violations and abuses against children and for the mitigation of violence fuelled by misinformation, disinformation and hate speech, and can be used to promote digital literacy and peace education and to amplify children’s voices, and also recognizing the need to address the digital divide, connectivity gaps and limited access to digital technologies for children affected by armed conflict, Expressing concern that disruptions of or restrictions on access to digital technologies and connectivity in situations of armed conflict may impede children’s access to education, humanitarian assistance, protection services and life-saving information, and may adversely affect the ability to document, report and prevent violations and abuses against children, Stressing that the best interests of the child and the specific needs and vulnerabilities of girls and boys, across different ages should be duly considered when planning and carrying out actions concerning children in situations of armed conflict, including in all actions regarding the provision, design, management and use of the digital environment, with appropriate safeguards to prevent harm, exploitation and abuse, while ensuring the protection of personal data, Stressing the importance of promoting awareness-raising, digital literacy and digital resilience to protect children from recruitment, use in hostilities and other exploitation by parties to armed conflict, including through digital technologies, and recognizing the role of States in providing access to inclusive and equitable education and digital skills that equip children to identify and report recruitment methods, and further noting efforts of Member States, including of Member States that have endorsed the Safe Schools Declaration, to facilitate the continuation of education during armed conflict, including when feasible, through distance learning and technological solutions, Recognizing the important role of regional and international partners in supporting Member States, upon request and in accordance with national ownership to strengthen child protection capacities, and to prevent violations and abuses against children in armed conflict, including when committed, facilitated or amplified through the use of digital technologies,

1. Strongly condemns all violations of applicable international law involving the recruitment and use of children by parties to armed conflict as well as their re‑recruitment, killing and maiming, rape and other forms of sexual violence, abductions, attacks against schools and hospitals as well as denial of humanitarian access by parties to armed conflict and all other violations of international law, including international humanitarian law, human rights law and refugee law, as well as human rights abuses committed against children in situations of armed conflict and demands that all relevant parties immediately put an end to such practices and take special measures to protect children;

2. Calls upon all parties to armed conflict, who are recruiting or using children in violation of the international obligations applicable to them, including through digital technologies, such as social media platforms, to immediately halt such recruitment, use or re-recruitment of children;

3. Stresses the important role of the Special Representative for Children and Armed Conflict in carrying out her mandate regarding the protection of children affected by armed conflict, in accordance with relevant Security Council resolutions, and stresses in particular, within the context of her mandate, the importance of facilitating further collaboration among United Nations partners at the field level and between the United Nations, including the UN Country Task Forces, and concerned Governments, in this regard requests the Special Representative to continue engaging proactively with UN agencies, Member States, regional and subregional organizations, and non‑state armed groups, and calls on the Special Representative, subject to the availability of resources, and together with relevant child protection actors, to compile comprehensive best practices, including for responding to violations and abuses against children in situations of armed conflict, committed, facilitated or amplified through the use of digital technologies;

4. Calls upon Member States to integrate into national child protection systems measures to reduce the risk of digital technologies being used to commit, facilitate or amplify violations and abuses against children, including, where appropriate, safe reporting and accessible, child-sensitive mechanisms to identify and provide appropriate services to children, survivor- and victim centred support, and safeguarding measures to prevent harm and re-victimisation and protect children from all forms of exploitation, and further encourages regional and international partners to assist Member States as appropriate, upon request;

5. Encourages Member States and relevant United Nations agencies as well as regional and international partners to strengthen coordination, cooperation, and investment in support of distance learning facilities, digital literacy and education in armed conflict and facilitating children’s access to digital infrastructure, technology and relevant skills, appropriate to their educational level, developmental and learning needs, and with psychosocial support and peer networks, including during the reintegration process, while working to prevent stigmatization and further encourages capacity-building support and assistance to developing countries, to close the digital divide across and within regions, while continuing to provide alternatives for those not reached by digital solutions, including low-connectivity solutions and recognizing that digital solutions should complement and not replace in-person child protection responses and education in conflict- affected settings;

6. Encourages Member States to ensure, when feasible, that teachers and educators are equipped with the competencies required to leverage technology in education, have access to digital resources and ensure that children affected by armed conflict, including children formerly associated with armed forces and armed groups, build digital literacy and resilience in order to reduce vulnerability to risks stemming from the digital environment, including through early identification of risks and appropriate child protection mechanisms and further encourages, where feasible, the production, adaptation and dissemination of safe and accessible digital resources in the education process to promote digital competencies, with the support of conducive policy and legal frameworks;

7. Encourages the Secretary General, in coordination with his Special Representative for Children and Armed Conflict, UNICEF, and relevant United Nations entities and child protection actors, in line with their respective mandates and subject to the availability of resources, to gather information and collect emerging lessons learned and best practices on the risks and benefits digital technologies present for the protection of children affected by armed conflict, including with regard to ending and preventing the recruitment and use and other violations and abuses committed, facilitated or amplified through digital technologies, and strengthening children’s digital literacy and safety, and, as appropriate, to reflect such lessons and practices in relevant reporting;

8. Calls on Member States to take appropriate measures consistent with obligations under international law to protect children in situations of armed conflict from violations and abuses committed, facilitated or amplified through digital technologies, encourages that the impact on children is put at the centre of digital policy-making and new initiatives related to the protection of children in armed conflict, including innovations that remain functional in low-connectivity and low‑resource environments, and further encourages Member States, where appropriate, to fully consider the specific needs and well-being of children in relevant digital initiatives with safeguards for privacy and data protection;

9. Stresses the importance of accountability for all violations and abuses against children in armed conflict and calls on States to continue to address impunity by efforts to strengthen national accountability mechanism, including building investigative and prosecutorial capacities, ensuring that those responsible for violations and abuses against children are brought to justice and held accountable without undue delay, including through timely and systematic investigation and prosecution, the results of which are made public, and ensure that all victims have access to justice as well as to the medical and support services they need;

10. Urges Member States to take action, consistent with applicable international law, against recruitment and use of children in armed conflict through the digital environment, including to prevent the use of children in malicious activities in the digital sphere, as well as the use of digital technologies for activities that may expose children to violations and abuses and to take appropriate measures to improve domestic compliance with obligations under international law, to end and prevent violations and abuses against children, including recruitment, use and re‑recruitment, abduction and rape and other forms of sexual violence, where committed, facilitated or amplified through the use of digital technologies, while noting that girls are at a higher risk of being subjected to violence facilitated or amplified through the use of digital technologies;

11. Calls upon Member States to enable national and regional research initiatives on the use of digital technologies in armed conflict in a manner that promotes affordable and accessible benefits for all, and assess benefits and risks of digital technologies for children, to prevent and mitigate harm caused to children through digital platforms and digital tools, including on mental health and well-being and safeguard the protection of children from violations and abuses, including by leveraging digital technologies;

12. Calls upon Member States to prevent recruitment and use and other violations and abuses against children in armed conflict by considering, where appropriate, fostering partnerships between governments and private sector with substantive safeguards to prevent harm, exploitation and abuse, and measures that may be taken to encourage providers of digital services that have children as end users or otherwise affect children, to design safe products that limit the exposure of children affected by armed conflict to inappropriate or harmful content or contact, including by adopting effective age assurance mechanisms and restricting access to violent or harmful content, to prevent, to the extent possible, the use of their products by parties to armed conflict to commit recruitment and use and other violations and abuses against children and to cooperate with the relevant child protection mechanisms to protect children in the digital environment;

13. Decides to remain actively seized of this matter.
